highlight.title: MCP 2026-07-28 Release Candidate: Stateless Core, MCP Apps, and Enterprise-Ready Extensions
highlight.summary: <cite index="1-2,1-4">The release candidate for MCP 2026-07-28 is now available, delivering the largest revision since launch with a stateless core, MCP Apps for server-rendered UIs, and authorization hardening.</cite> <cite index="1-9,1-12">Key production impacts include required Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers for load balancer routing, plus new ttlMs and cacheScope fields for intelligent caching without long-lived SSE streams.</cite>

resources.title: NSA Security Design Considerations for MCP
resources.why_now: <cite index="9-4,9-12">Recent research shows semantic and tool poisoning in MCP as systemic threats, while the security posture remains uneven and dependent on implementation discipline rather than protocol guarantees.</cite>

resources.title: OpenCode Takes #1 Spot in AI Coding Agent Rankings
resources.why_now: <cite index="14-1,14-13">OpenCode entered at #1 with 160K+ GitHub stars and 7.5M monthly developers, becoming the most-adopted open-source coding agent with model-agnostic access to 75+ providers.</cite>

resources.title: MCP Enterprise Adoption Forecast: 38-46% of Fortune 1000
resources.why_now: <cite index="23-9,23-11">Enterprise deployment rate decides whether MCP becomes the standard, with base forecast showing 38-46% Fortune 1000 adoption by Q3 end—crossing 50% locks in standardization.</cite>

resources.title: Claude Code Dominates Developer Survey at 46% Love Rate
resources.why_now: <cite index="11-14,31-32">Claude Code went from zero to #1 AI coding tool in 8 months, especially loved by senior leadership (Director+), while 95% of respondents now use AI tools weekly.</cite>

claude_take: MCP is rapidly converging toward the de facto standard for AI-system integration, but the 3-6 month window is critical—enterprise adoption rates will determine whether it locks in or fragments. The shift from stateful to stateless architecture plus MCP Apps signals enterprise-production readiness, while security concerns from NSA and tool poisoning research show the protocol needs hardening before widespread deployment. Expect consolidation around MCP + terminal-native agents as the dominant pattern.
